## 1 Introduction

This micro case illustrates what instrumental variables actually identify when
treatment effects are heterogeneous. While IV estimators are often interpreted
as estimating the average treatment effect (ATE), in general they identify the
Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE).

## 2 Data Generating Process

We simulate a population consisting of never-takers, compliers, and always-takers.
The instrument affects treatment assignment only for compliers, satisfying
monotonicity and exclusion restrictions.

```{r dgp}
set.seed(123)

n <- 3000
u <- rnorm(n)

type <- sample(
  c("never", "complier", "always"),
  size = n,
  replace = TRUE,
  prob = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.3)
)

z <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)

treat <- ifelse(
  type == "never", 0,
  ifelse(type == "always", 1, z)
)

y0 <- 5 + u + rnorm(n)
tau <- ifelse(type == "complier", 4, 1)
y1 <- y0 + tau

y <- y0 + treat * (y1 - y0)

case3C <- data.frame(y, treat, z, type, y0, y1, tau)
```

## 3 True ATE vs True LATE

```{r true-effects}
ATE  <- mean(case3C$y1 - case3C$y0)
LATE <- mean(case3C$tau[case3C$type == "complier"])

c(ATE = ATE, LATE = LATE)
```

## 4 OLS Benchmark

```{r ols}
ols <- lm(y ~ treat, data = case3C)
summary(ols)
```

## 5 IV Estimation

```{r iv-wald}
wald <- cov(case3C$y, case3C$z) / cov(case3C$treat, case3C$z)
wald
```

```{r iv-2sls}
library(AER)
iv <- ivreg(y ~ treat | z, data = case3C)
summary(iv)
```

## 6 Who Are the Compliers?


### 6.1 Compliance Types in the Population

```{r compliance-plot}
type_counts <- table(case3C$type)
barplot(
  type_counts / sum(type_counts),
  col = c("gray70", "steelblue", "gray40"),
  main = "Compliance Types in the Population",
  ylab = "Share"
)
```

```{r compliers}
p1 <- mean(case3C$treat[case3C$z == 1])
p0 <- mean(case3C$treat[case3C$z == 0])

c(
  Share_Compliers = p1 - p0,
  True_Share_Compliers = mean(case3C$type == "complier")
)
```

## 7 Policy Interpretation


**Policy note.**  
The IV estimate identifies the effect of treatment for *compliers*—individuals
whose treatment status is changed by the instrument. This Local Average Treatment
Effect (LATE) need not coincide with the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) relevant
for large-scale policy interventions, especially when treatment effects are
heterogeneous.

The IV estimate should be interpreted as the effect of treatment for those whose
treatment status is changed by the instrument.

## 8 Conclusion

This case shows that IV estimators identify the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE)
when treatment effects are heterogeneous.
